I'm examining the Document class to plan test coverage, focusing on the constructor, createShell's null validation, the head/body accessors, and both branches of title() getting and setting—particularly how it handles a missing title element.

I also need to cover normalise() and its private helpers through observable behavior, OutputSettings' escape mode, charset, pretty print, and indent amount validation, plus outerHtml, text, and nodeName methods. I'm sketching out concrete test method names like testCreateShellNullBaseUri and testTitle_whenNoTitleElement to ensure each branch, including edge cases where head or body don't exist, gets explicit coverage.

For testing the null-structure branches, I need to figure out how to construct a bare Document that lacks html/head/body elements, since the constructor creates one with a "#root" tag by default.

Tracing through normalise() for such an empty document: head()/body() both return null since there are no children to match against, so the tag search falls through correctly. Then normalise() would detect the missing html element, append it, prepend a head, and append a body in sequence, which confirms the expected branch coverage for that test case.

For a partial document with only html and body already present, normalise() should skip creating a duplicate body but still prepend the missing head, which I need to verify against the branch logic.

Now I want to test moving loose text nodes: starting from a shell document with html/head/body already structured, I'll attach a stray TextNode directly to the document root, then call normalise() and check that it gets relocated into the body with correct ordering, since the move logic iterates childNodes and prepends.

I should also check that normaliseTextNodes skips blank-only text nodes, meaning they're not moved into the body at all. To verify this, I'll craft a test where a blank TextNode is placed directly in head's child nodes before calling normalise, then confirm body's content doesn't pick up any extra whitespace from it.

Rather than trying to assume the exact internal defect being tested (likely related to how normalise handles text ordering or indentation), I'll keep the tests grounded in the documented spec and avoid over-specifying fragile internal behaviors. I also want to add coverage for OutputSettings defaults, starting with checking what escapeMode() returns by default.

I should also verify that setting and getting escapeMode round-trips correctly, that the default charset is UTF-8, and that updating the charset propagates to the encoder -- though since encoder() is package-private, I'll need DocumentTest to live in org.jsoup.nodes to access it, matching the real Defects4j test setup.

For indentAmount, I'll check the default is 1, confirm 0 and positive values work, and that negative values throw IllegalArgumentException via Validate.isTrue. I'll also verify prettyPrint defaults to true and can be toggled off, then move into testing Element methods like appendElement, appendChild, prependChild, prependElement, and the text setter.

Element extends from Document and has standard jsoup API methods like text(), getElementsByTag, html(), nodeName() - this should all compile fine given it's an older jsoup version. Now I'm sketching out the first concrete test case, verifying the constructor sets baseUri and nodeName correctly.

For the next tests, I'm checking that createShell properly builds the html/head/body structure, and that passing a null base URI to createShell throws the expected validation exception.

Then I'm planning cases where head() and body() return null when the document lacks those elements, title() returns an empty string on a shell doc, and title() returns trimmed text when a title element exists. I also want to cover setTitle adding a title to the head when none exists yet.

I should test that setting title updates existing text without duplicating the title element, verify that setting a null title throws an exception, and add a basic createElement test using a Document and Element.

Then I plan test cases for normalising an empty document—checking it creates html, head, and body—and for when html exists but head is missing, ensuring normalise adds the missing head.

I'm also covering cases where body is missing and verifying it gets appended, plus a test confirming a stray text node at the document root gets moved into the body during normalisation.

Next I'm adding a test to confirm blank text nodes are skipped during normalisation, leaving the body text empty rather than inserting whitespace content.

Then I'm planning a test for outerHtml output, verifying it includes an html tag and isn't wrapped oddly like a document node, followed by a test confirming doc.text("Hello World") correctly sets the body text, and starting a nodeName test.

Next I'm sketching out a series of OutputSettings tests covering default escape mode, setting escape mode, default UTF-8 charset, setting the charset by object or name, default pretty print behavior, toggling pretty print off, and default/custom indent amounts.

I'm also considering a test for the package-private encoder() method, checking that it matches the charset's encoder by comparing charset names rather than relying on CharsetEncoder equality—something like verifying that setting the charset to ISO-8859-1 produces an encoder reporting that same name.

Now I'm turning to how Validate.isTrue behaves.

I still need the remaining two branch combinations: html present but head missing, and html present but body missing. I should also add a test confirming that when all three elements already exist, normalise() doesn't duplicate anything, checking that only one html, head, and body tag remain after calling it on a shell document.

For the title-related branches, I've covered the null-title case, the present-title case, the null-check assignment, the else branch, and the Validate.notNull failure case. Now I'm ready to write the actual test file, making sure I only import what's needed—Charset for the charset tests, JUnit's Test annotation—since the node classes are in the same package already.

Let me verify the Element API I'm relying on: appendElement, prependElement, getElementsByTag returning Elements with first() and size(), the text() getter/setter, tagName(), parent(), and baseUri() from Node rather than a baseUrl() method. I also want to confirm Elements inherits List.size() and that child(int) works for checking element order, like verifying a prepended head tag ends up at index 0. I'm also double-checking whether childNodes() is publicly accessible versus being a protected field the source accesses directly.

I'll keep the test assertions grounded in the given source plus the standard jsoup API without over-assuming version-specific details. For the TextNode constructor, I'm confirming it takes text and baseUri, matching usage inside the source itself. For the Validate exception type, I'll either wrap calls in a try/catch with fail() for safety or just assume IllegalArgumentException is thrown, since that's the conventional choice for Validate.isTrue failures.

Now I'm writing out the full test class, adding boundary tests for blank baseUri (should not throw since notNull only rejects null, not empty) and empty title strings (should also succeed), then compiling a summary explanation.
